summary: Reinhard Heydrich, a cashiered German naval officer, built the SS intelligence service, ran the Gestapo and Nazi police terror, led the Einsatzgruppen and chaired the Wannsee Conference that organised the Holocaust before his 1942 assassination in Prague.

evidence.note: Birth in Halle, Prussia, 1904; father's career and childhood follow
Wartime blockade and Kaiser-era navy propaganda shape his youth
Court-martialed over broken engagement and discharged from the navy in 1931
Himmler hires him to build an SS intelligence service; founding of the SD
Redefines protective custody to detain without courts; Dachau intake
Fabricated dossier against Roehm leads to the Night of the Long Knives
His proposals at the 1935 meeting feed directly into the Nuremberg Laws
SS teams arrest opponents and seize Jewish property after the Anschluss
Einsatzgruppen liquidation lists and massacres during the invasion of Poland
Mass shootings at Babi Yar near Kyiv and in Odessa
Acting Reich Protector in Bohemia-Moravia; ambushed and dies of sepsis 1942
Lidice reprisal: men shot, children gassed

notes: Roles medium: navy service gets a long Part 1 segment (military-officer would also fit) but the story centres on his SD/Gestapo and Reich Protector roles. Lina Heydrich (nee von Osten) gets her own segment as a driver of his Nazi turn. Lidice reprisals right after his death kept inside 1942.
